postSubmit.note: Message and Redirect; Message has a text box with Thank you!, Alignment and Position with three each, and an HTML code box. Redirect has Attach link. What these draw after a submit is not read: a submit writes to form storage.

canvas.note: While the view is open the block shows what comes after a submit. The form stays in the same grid cell, hidden, and sets the height, block and rows unchanged. The Submit word stays showing, white, with no button behind it. The text box is rich text, HTML a code editor. Both views show the message. On Back the form returns.

html.note: Drawn as HTML under the message, not aligned with it.

attachLink.note: The link menu with URL and the site list. What the row shows after a link is set: not read.

messageBox.note: The Message box is rich text with a short bar, on a new form on the probe page, not saved. Squarespace AI was never pressed.

box.focus: 2px solid rgb(14, 14, 14), and none after leaving
box.grows: A second and third line take the inner box from 22 to 58 and 80. Its outer height with many lines is not read.

bar.shows: On focus, gone on leaving the box.

marks.selection: Bold draws strong, Italic em, Underline u, inside the p, nested strong > em > u. A second press takes the mark off. The selection stays.
marks.boldCaret: Bold at a caret marks all the text. Italic at a caret marks it and takes it off.
marks.underlineCaret: Underline at a caret changes no text: the next letter typed is not underlined when the caret was in underlined text. The other way round is inferred from Strike in a Text block.
marks.clear: Clear Formatting takes all marks off the selection and leaves it.
marks.enter: Enter makes a new p. Shift+Enter a br in it.

styles.menu: Rows 44 high with the keys, as the Text block lists them, under the bar. The current one has a tick. Pressing a row keeps the selection and closes the list.

link.press: The same link menu as a Text block, 328 wide, centred under the Link button and 6 below it, with the list open. Link shows pressed while it is open.
link.write: Enter leaves the menu open, with the list gone, and writes nothing yet. A press away closes it, writes the a around the marks, gives the box its focus and selection back, and the bar stays. Link shows pressed on the selection, and not at a caret in the link.

messageBox.empty: Emptied, the box shows Thank you! as a faded placeholder and Link fades. The block draws no message at all.
messageBox.escape: Escape in the box closes the whole panel.
messageBox.shape: The stored html carries attributes of their editor. Ours keeps the tags and the two paragraph classes.
messageBox.notRead: Heading 2 and 3 in the box (browser defaults assumed). Pasting into the box: ours takes plain text. Cmd+I and Cmd+U: Cmd+B was read, the others assumed.

lightbox.note: On: the form leaves and a button named Open Form takes its place, 204 by 67; the rows Button Text and Background Color appear and the Background, Stroke, Blend Mode and Blur rows go. Button Text is empty with Open Form as its placeholder. Stretch leaves the button its own width, at the left. Off: the form comes back. A press on the button in the preview of an unsaved form opened nothing, twice, so what the open lightbox draws is not read: under 0005, because it needs a Save.

css.font: 16px, weight 500, letter spacing 0.32px, line height normal, 25px measured

styles.note: Secondary and Tertiary change the class to sqs-button-element--secondary or --tertiary. The box and rows hold. On this site all three read black on white.

typed.note: From a 1-row block: stays 1 row, the height did not change.

long.text: A rather long label on this button that should run wider than the block it sits in, and then some more words

picked.note: A swatch changes the row and adds Reset to theme. The button and the block do not change: the color belongs to what opens.

off.note: The rows stay and the form overflows them, stretching the grid: 3 rows read 560.9 high.

refit.note: The next Button Alignment press gives the form its rows.

on2.note: From 14 rows: 1 row, stretched by the button.

fewerFields.note: Message deleted on a new form, rows not yet settled at 16. Still 3 rows.

fieldDeleteWhileOn.note: A field deleted while on leaves the rows and the button alone.

up70.note: 3 rows dragged up by 70: stops at 2, the least that holds the button.

reads.contentTab: The Content tab does not change: Form Name, its own Button Text, Edit Form Fields and the rest.
reads.colorPop: The five swatches, the plus and the Opacity slider. White is chosen at the start and no Reset to theme shows.

lightbox.rowRule: On: the rows lose ceil((form height - button height) / row pitch), with a floor of 1. Read four times: 16 rows and a 560.9 form to 3, 14 and 560.9 to 1, 11 and 410.5 to 2, and 16 and 410.5 to 3. That last one had a field deleted with the rows not yet settled, so the rule fits it only if the height is the one from before the delete. Off: the rows stay until the next press on a design row (offThenPress). Typing moves the rows only when the button's height changes, then to the least that hold it. Alignment never shrinks them.

deleteThenOn.note: Tested on the lead's question: does the older height count? One delete holds: 16 rows and a 410.5 form go to 3 like a 560.9 form, also after waiting 8 seconds. More deletes don't fit it. Two deletes: 12 rows, form 315.7, go to 2, a loss of 10, while the older heights give 13, 9 or 7. Three deletes: 9 rows, form 189.1, go to 1. No height before the delete explains all of them, so it isn't built.

offThenPress.note: After Lightbox off, the first press on Button Alignment or Button Style grows the rows to hold the form. It never shrinks them. Without a Lightbox off first, a press does nothing to the rows, also when they are short. It is one view at a time.

submissions.manage: A link to the Contacts page's form submitters, in a new tab. Read by going there: an empty list with Email, First Name, Last Name, Total Submissions, Last Submission and Email Subscribed.
submissions.export: A press fades the row for a moment. No dialog, nothing else on screen. No submissions are stored on the trial site.

menu.note: An option's menu has two rows on every field kind read: Radio, Checkbox, Dropdown and Survey. An option left alone still has Delete Option. Capitals, 12px, weight 500, letter spacing 0.5px. Delete Option is rgb(195, 45, 56). The earlier note of one row in this finding was my wrong read of a menu that runs past the panel's bottom: the screenshot from that run shows both rows.

box.position: Right edge 4 left of the button, top 40 under the button's top. It may run past the panel's bottom.

delete.note: Delete Option removes the option at once, with no dialog, from the menu or from Option Details. Its follow-ups go with it. Options can all go: the field then draws its legend alone, 30.4 high. Add option then adds Option 1.

option.withFollowUp: A row to open in place of the field and the menu: name, then n follow-up under it, 16 high, and an arrow. 61 high, so Add option moves up 4.
option.plural: Follow-up with one, Follow-ups with more. Rows 67 apart.

followUp.tile: A tile adds the follow-up and opens its editor. Nothing new draws on the canvas while editing.

back.deleteField: Delete Field goes to the field, from either route.
back.lastDeleted: With its last follow-up gone the option is a plain row with its menu again.

drawn.note: In Preview. They draw at once after the field, 32 in and 486 wide, 20 apart, in option order however they were picked. Another radio takes them away. The select was set by script with a change event, not by a press.
drawn.dropdownPress: A real press on the Dropdown in Preview focuses it and shows no list in the page: nothing new in the document, not :open, and arrow keys and Enter after it left the first option picked. It's a native select, whose list a headless Chrome doesn't draw. So what the list looks like is unread. Picking by script with a change event is how the option rule was read.

survey.note: A survey's option offers follow-ups and draws them. A rating on an option's row draws that option's follow-ups, after the whole survey, in option order however they were rated. A survey has no way to unpick a rating, so they stay. An earlier note here said a first rating drew nothing: that press missed, because the page was still scrolling when I measured. The later reads checked the rating was checked.

followUp.blockRows: While a tile is pressed the rows can read tall for a moment, as in blockFits.

marks.tick: A picked checkbox shows a tick in a 12px box in the 20px circle, in the text color. Ours draws its own tick: the shape is ours, not the oracle's. It wipes in from the left: 0.2s, after 0.1s, cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1), read frame by frame to end at about 0.3s.
marks.dot: A picked radio or rating shows an 8px dot in the middle, in the text color. It scales from 0 to 1 over 0.1s, after 0.1s, on the same curve, read frame by frame to end at about 0.2s.
marks.circle: At rest 1px in the text color, 20 across. Hover, without focus: 2px inward, the same color. Focus, with or without a hover, by a press or by script, picked or not: 2px inward in the site's accent, rgb(242, 184, 180) here. Radio and checkbox read alike. A radio's and a checkbox's edge move over border-width 0.075s and border-color 0.2s. Focus elsewhere puts it back.

transitions.edge: border-width 0.075s cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1), border-color 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1), transform 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1)

ringByTheme.note: The focus ring read in Preview on a new form on the probe page, on a checkbox and a radio, on all ten section themes. Checkbox and radio read the same. That the two Bright colors are the palette colors of those values is inferred: one palette was read.

followUp.backFromMenu: Back from Add Follow-Up, reached by an option's menu, goes to the field's view, as ours does.

undo: Undo did not step back a field's change. After adding a Dropdown one Undo left it there; after typing a label and a description one Undo left both, and the next removed the whole Form block. Ours takes one step per change.
presses: The press on the lightbox button in the preview checked the element on top inside the frame.
The row drag in the list checked the row was on top at its start.

The bottom edge drag on the Lightbox block was by coordinates, read from the block's box. Every other press in the Lightbox reads checked the element on top; the Button Style list was pressed on the element found on top at the label's center.

Follow-up reads: radio, checkbox, rating and Dropdown presses in Preview checked the control on top inside the frame and that its place had stopped moving. A hover read moved the pointer to the same place. Every other press used the on-top helper.
notRead: What a form's open lightbox draws: the preview opens nothing on an unsaved form, and it needs a Save (under 0005).
What the Message, Alignment, Position, HTML and Redirect do after a submit: a submit writes to form storage.
Send confirmation email and SMS Marketing Opt-in: not pressed. View plans: not pressed.
Email Notification, Additional Storage, reCAPTCHA: not pressed.

oursDiffers: The block's rows fit in the same step as a change. The oracle settles a step late on add, duplicate, delete and toggles: reads in blockFits.
A typed value fits when the field is left. The oracle did not change rows for typing while the panel stayed in the field.
One undo step per change. The oracle's Undo did not step field changes back: reads in undo.
The Country list is the browser's region names, 251 of them, with Norway chosen. The oracle has 245. The Phone prefix stays +47.
The field and tile icons are our own drawings.
Ours' HTML box has no colours or code editor. It takes the same text.
In ours' Preview frame a redirect shows the message, so the editor stays open. On the page itself it follows the link.
A form with a field just deleted: ours has already fit its rows, so Lightbox on reads from there. The oracle's rows had not settled (lightbox, reads.otherForm.fewerFields: 3 rows where ours gives 2).

What the Lightbox button opens is ours, with no read behind it: a dark page, a 640 wide box in the chosen Background Color, the form and a close button. A press beside the box or on the close button ends it. The text and submit button turn black or white to read on the color.
Ours has no tooltip Open menu on an option's menu button.
On the phone too the rows fit in the same step. The oracle's fit is one step late there as well.
Lightbox off from the phone keeps 16 rows every time. The oracle read 15 in two of six reads on the same route, and a press gives 17 either way.
A phone form turned on from desktop, off and on again from the phone: ours goes to 1 row by the height it draws, the oracle to 2 by the 549 block.
The Message box takes plain text on a paste. The oracle's paste is not read.
inferred: Hidden's Variable follows the Label: only SQF_HIDDEN for the label Hidden was read.
A grip on an option moves the option: only the field list's drag was read.
The Name part hidden by Show keeps its Require value for when it comes back.
A real submit draws the message as the view does, and the Submit word goes.
A message taller than the form: not read.
Background Color belongs to what the Lightbox button opens: nothing on the canvas changes when it is picked, and the open view is not read.
Lightbox on leaves a Background, Stroke, Blend Mode or Blur set earlier on the block as it was: only new forms were read, with none of them set.
Ours hides the follow-ups again on leaving Preview, and a field's picks stay.

checkboxGap.note: Read on the Contact page and on a form added to a probe page. Ours: imported fields keep 14, tile-made Checkbox and Radio use 18. Why they differ, and which a Checkbox added to the Contact form takes, is not read.

phone.note: Phone view, 428 wide. A new form is 16 rows there too, 376.7 wide. Fields keep their order and draw at the column's width. Address stacks Postal Code and City / Town. Fields work the same in the phone's panel.
phone.rows: Rows are per view. A field added on the phone moves only the phone's rows, one step late as on desktop, and desktop's rows stay and stretch to hold the form. A field added on desktop leaves the phone's rows, which stretch.
phone.perView: Lightbox, its Button Text and Background Color, Button Alignment and Button Style are per view, one key at a time. The phone follows desktop on a key until the phone changes that key, and then keeps it. A desktop change leaves a key the phone has changed. Read: phone Right, then desktop Center keeps phone Right; phone Lightbox on leaves desktop's off; phone Right, then desktop Lightbox on: the phone shows the button, on the right; desktop's Button Text reaches a phone that has not typed one; a phone's Go stays when desktop's is Open Form; phone Secondary leaves desktop Primary and desktop Tertiary leaves phone Secondary; desktop Secondary reaches a phone that has not chosen; a phone swatch leaves desktop white and a desktop swatch leaves the phone's.
phone.lightboxRows: Lightbox on from the phone: the rule as on desktop, with the phone's pitch of 35: 16 rows and 562.7 go to 1 by the floor. Desktop's rows stay. Lightbox on from desktop: the phone's rows stay at 16 and the button sits at the top of a 549 block. Off from the phone, with Lightbox on from desktop: read six times with no press between, 16 rows four times and 15 twice, on the same route. No wait explains it, and a press gives 17 from either. On again after that: 2 rows, not 1, the 549 height counting. Both are named in oursDiffers.
